source: Subjects were instructed to classify the pictures as living or nonliving by pressing one of two response buttons with their dominant hand.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Stimuli were displayed for 2 s, with an inter-stimulus interval jittered between 1.7 and 2.1 s.
source: Stimuli were displayed for 2 s, with an inter-stimulus interval jittered between 1.7 and 2.1 s.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental timing, also shown in Figure 1a.

claim: A total of 170 trials were presented: each individual stimulus was repeated 2.5 times in a random order.
source: A total of 170 trials were presented: each individual stimulus was repeated 2.5 times in a random order.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Data from one outlier in the svPPA cohort were excluded from the behavioral analyses.
source: Data from one outlier in the svPPA cohort were excluded from the behavioral analyses (average reaction times were 1.35 s vs. 0.8 s in the whole cohort).
evidence: This is a description of data exclusion criteria.

claim: Structural T1-weighted images were acquired on a 3 T Siemens system.
source: Structural T1-weighted images were acquired on a 3 T Siemens system (Siemens, Erlagen, Germany) installed at the UCSF Neuroscience Imaging Center, equipped with a standard quadrature head coil with sequences previously described (Mandelli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a description of the MRI acquisition protocol.

claim: MRI scans were acquired within 1 year of the MEG data acquisition.
source: MRI scans were acquired within 1 year of the MEG data acquisition.
evidence: This is a description of the temporal relationship between data acquisitions.

claim: To identify regions of atrophy, svPPA patients were compared to a separate set of 25 HC via voxel-based morphometry (VBM).
source: To identify regions of atrophy, svPPA patients were compared to a separate set of 25 HC collected using the same protocol (14 females, mean age 66.2 ± 8.5) via voxel-based morphometry (VBM).
evidence: This is a description of the VBM analysis procedure.

claim: Neuromagnetic recordings were conducted using a whole-head 275 axial gradiometer MEG system at a sampling rate of 1200 Hz.
source: Neuromagnetic recordings were conducted using a whole-head 275 axial gradiometer MEG system (Omega 2000, CTF, Coquitlam, BC, Canada) at a sampling rate of 1200 Hz, under a bandpass filter of 0.001–300 Hz, while subjects performed the task.
evidence: This is a description of the MEG acquisition parameters.

claim: All subjects included in the study exhibited movement under 1 cm.
source: All subjects included in the current study exhibited movement under 1 cm, as measured pre- and post- experimental run.
evidence: This is a description of data quality control.

claim: The two cohorts did not differ in average motion level: svPPA 0.28 cm (SD 0.11), HC 0.39 cm (SD 0.22) (p=0.12).
source: The two cohorts did not differ in average motion level: svPPA 0.28 cm (SD 0.11), HC 0.39 cm (SD 0.22) (p=0.12).
evidence: This is a statistical result comparing motion between groups.

claim: Mean number of trials included in analyses for the two groups did not significantly differ (svPPA mean = 155 trials, control mean = 162, p=0.297).
source: Mean number of trials included in analyses for the two groups did not significantly differ (svPPA mean = 155 trials [SD = 20, range 121–170], control mean = 162 [SD = 16, range 103–172], two-tailed t[34]=1.059, p=0.297).
evidence: This is a statistical result comparing trial numbers between groups.

claim: Reconstruction of whole brain oscillatory activity was performed via the Neurodynamic Utility Toolbox for MEG (NUTMEG).
source: Reconstruction of whole brain oscillatory activity within these voxels was performed via the Neurodynamic Utility Toolbox for MEG (NUTMEG; http://nutmeg.berkeley.edu, Hinkley et al., 2020), which implements a time-frequency optimized adaptive spatial filtering technique to estimate the spatiotemporal estimate of neural sources.
evidence: This is a description of the MEG analysis method.

claim: The beamforming algorithm chosen was a variant of the synthetic aperture magnetometry (SAM) inverse solution.
source: The beamforming algorithm choses was a variant of the synthetic aperture magnetometry (SAM) inverse solution (Vrba and Robinson, 2001) as implemented in NUTMEG (Hinkley et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a description of the source localization method, supported by citations.

claim: Five frequency bands were examined: theta (3–7 Hz), alpha (8–12 Hz), beta (12–30 Hz), low-gamma (30–55 Hz), and high-gamma (63–117 Hz).
source: Thus, we examined task-related modulations of ongoing oscillatory processes in five frequency bands: theta (3–7 Hz), alpha (8–12 Hz), beta (12–30 Hz), low-gamma (30–55 Hz), and high-gamma (63–117 Hz) (FIR filter having widths of 300 ms for theta/alpha, 200 ms for beta, 150 ms for low-gamma, and 100 ms for high-gamma; sliding over 25 ms time windows).
evidence: This is a description of the frequency band analysis parameters.
